findings.key_quote: The effective tax rate decreased from the three months ended September 30, 2025 to the three months ended September 30, 2026.
findings.justification: This passage explicitly states that the effective tax rate decreased (not increased) for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to the prior year quarter. The effective tax rate was 20.5% in Q3 2025 and 18.2% in Q3 2026, showing a decrease. This directly contradicts the claim that the effective tax rate increased.

findings.key_quote: The decrease is primarily attributed to lower pre-tax earnings from unrealized losses on equity securities that are deferred tax assets at statutory tax rates, an increase in the foreign-derived deduction eligible income tax deduction, and less non-deductible fines, partially offset by changes in prior period tax positions.
findings.justification: This passage explains the causes of the effective tax rate decrease for the three months ended September 30, 2026. It does not mention stock-based compensation (SBC) tax benefits as a cause. The passage is about the correct period but addresses causes different from those claimed, making it related but not deciding on the specific causation asserted in the claim.

findings.key_quote: The increase is primarily attributed to higher pre-tax earnings from unrealized gains on equity securities that are deferred tax liabilities at the statutory tax rate, and an increase in acquisition-related tax integration costs, partially offset by an increase in SBC-related tax benefits and foreign-derived deduction eligible income tax deduction.
findings.justification: This passage discusses the nine months ended September 30, 2026 (not the three months/quarter), so it addresses a different period than the claim. While it mentions SBC-related tax benefits increased (which would lower, not raise, the effective tax rate), this is for the nine-month period, not the quarter specified in the claim.

This derived metric shows that operating margin increased by approximately 1.29 percentage points from Q3 2025 to Q3 2026 (from 30.51% to 31.81%). The assertion N1 states 'OperatingMargin level increase None', which means no increase occurred. The evidence shows an increase did occur, contradicting the assertion.

Operating income of $40,576 million and revenue of $127,577 million for Q3 2026 yield an operating margin of 31.8% (40,576/127,577). Combined with the comparison period figures (E9, E10), this shows operating margin increased from 30.5% to 31.8%, contradicting the assertion that there was no increase.

Operating income of $31,228 million and revenue of $102,346 million for Q3 2025 yield an operating margin of 30.5% (31,228/102,346). This comparison period figure, when combined with Q3 2026 figures, demonstrates that operating margin increased, contradicting the assertion of no increase.
